body: - **Integration:** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs`, one file per behaviour, depending only on dev-dependencies; the stand checks read the tables and helpers they share from `tests/common/mod.rs` (`mod common;`) and the checks that hold a session — the session checks, `stand_settle`, the sixteen driver-action checks `stand_act_*`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `stand_screenshot_repeat`, `stand_requirement_sweep`, `stand_virtual_clock`, since 2026-10-19-session-recording `stand_session_recording` and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, `stand_replay` and, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, `stand_lint` and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_load_wait` and, since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `stand_snapshot_parts` and the two served-page checks `stand_cells_served` and `stand_load_page` (35 readers, `stand_cells_served` and `stand_load_page` the thirtieth and thirty-first, `stand_act_popup` the thirty-second, `stand_graph` the thirty-third, `stand_actions` the thirty-fourth, `stand_handler_coverage` the thirty-fifth; `stand_mcp_masked`, `password_painted_masked`, `stand_non_lean_tasks` and `password_caret_click` declare none) — what they share from `tests/session_common/mod.rs` (`mod session_common;`: the held session, the driver's call builders `click` · `type_into` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` · `snapshot` · `screenshot` · `screenshot_of` · `lint` · `graph` · `snapshot_part`, the outcome reader `act`, the part reader `part` (a paged snapshot's text, part and count), the shot reader `shot`, the lint reader `linted` (a lint's findings), the graph reader `graphed` (a graph's `UiGraph`), the refusal readers `refused` and `refused_unchanged`, since 2026-10-19-session-recording the recording readers `kept` and the unix-only `mode`, and since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `shot_prefix` (the first 64 base64 characters of a whole-screen shot) — its `replay` removed then for the replay `Check::replay`); and, since 2026-10-19-shared-fixtures, what 32 checks — 24 `stand_*` files (`stand_snapshot_parts` since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `stand_act_select`, `stand_load_wait` since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_lint` since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, `stand_act_popup`, `stand_actions`), `font_face_sniffed_source`, `select_interaction`, `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted`, `inert_subtree`, `accessibility_states`, `checkable_change_event` and `text_range_no_change_event` — share from `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (`mod fixtures;`, `#![allow(dead_code)]`: the fixture boot `boot(app, incremental)` with the stand's options `stand::options(incremental)`, `hold(label, app, incremental)` over it, the pages more than one check reads — `password_labelled`, `password_named`, `covered` and `many_items` with its `ITEMS` (read by `stand_snapshot_parts` and `stand_act_spans`) — and the held network stand-in `HeldNet`); none is a test target. Every other file is its own target: `tests/all.rs` is upstream's single-binary target, kept in the manifest at `test = false` and never built — add no `autotests = false` and no second `[[test]]` table (`BlitzTestsTargetsTest`, in the `ci-scripts` leg, pins it). A check that needs a session process starts and stops its own host (its test binary re-run on one `#[ignore]` child, or the package's binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`), bounds every wait, guards the host with kill-and-reap and, holding a session over the socket, is `cfg(unix)`-gated — a check that drives the `escher-session mcp` stdio child (`mcp_server`, `mcp_log`) does it through the shared `Speaker` (piped stdin, stdout read line by line on a thread under a 30 s bound, kill-and-reap in its `Drop`) and is not unix-gated but `mcp_server`'s two command-line comparisons; since 2026-10-19-session-recording a check that records is `cfg(unix)`-gated item by item, in-process and `mcp` stdio ones included (`mcp_log`'s recorded test), beside an off-unix check that a recording is refused `Unsupported`, which the windows job alone runs; a host ends by itself after its idle expiry, so a check that waits for one watches the state directory — an `attach` or a `status` is an answered request and starts the count again. The seven_guis checks also run the `escher-session` binary once per command as a client and read its stdout, stderr and exit status (`0` · `1` · `2` · `3`) through `tests/common/mod.rs`, which since 2026-10-19-test-splits also states the log checks' fragment once — `Needles` and `stand_needles` (the CRUD stand's id and name needles), `stamped_lines`, `found`, `occurrences`, the unix-only `recorded_needles` and `cells_needles(part)` (part `part`'s author keys of the in-process Cells screen and the middle column-A cell it holds) — called by `host_log` and `mcp_log` alone, `option_needles()` (the needle list of a select's options read from a snapshot), called by the same two, and `graph_needles()` (the component and state names of the UI graph as needles), called by the same two, and `actions_needles()` (the CRUD screen's listed author-key ids holding a `-` as needles), called by the same two, and `coverage_needles()` (the CRUD screen's UI-graph ids and names as needles), called by `host_log` alone; the two flows under `tests/flows/` are POSIX `sh` scripts run by the Rust target `cli_flow` and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, a third, `record_checks.sh`, by seven_guis `recording`'s unix-gated `the_committed_checks_are_what_the_binary_records` — assets of a `cargo test` target, not a runner of their own.

- 2026-11-09: When a test joins a check file whose tests the masters or leaves name by ordinal (`host_log`'s fourth test), append it after the named ones or sweep the ordinal phrasings too — an insertion above shifts every later ordinal, and a sweep keyed on test names and counts reads none of them.

Where a root ReachedRecord context stands, the record is written after the event-kind and dioxus-id early returns and before runtime.handle_event, and every other document pays one has_context lookup per dispatch.

CLIs contract and the driver's command line: the role set of escher-session (serve host role and mcp role) gains a third, coverage, with its own usage-line clause. The exit statuses stay 0, 1, 2 and 3, none added.

Driver session decision (crossing boundary): a kept check named on the coverage role's argv and read from the caller's files is a ratified boundary widening (pattern rul-izni57qv, the founder's word). It adds no socket, no port, no env read and no carrier.

escher-driver's public handler_coverage(checks, boot) boots a fresh session per check, skips a check whose app is not the label, switches on record_reached, reads the UI graph at boot and after each replayed step (mounted left out, deduplicated by id and event), and returns Coverage { unexercised: Vec<HandlerRef>, checks, held }, HandlerRef { id, owner, event }, its line {"unexercised":[...],"checks":n,"held":m}.

dioxus-native-dom's ungated reached module exposes ReachedHandler { id, event }, DioxusDocument::record_reached (provides a crate-private ReachedRecord at ScopeId::ROOT, a second call keeping the one record) and reached_handlers (handlers in first-reached order, deduplicated by id and event, empty when never switched on); the record's Debug prints its count alone.

The reached record inserts, for each node of a dispatch's chain whose current listeners hold the event's name, that node's stable id resolved at dispatch, so a handler whose own run removes its element still counts; it reads the crate-private ungated element_listener_ids, one vdom walk of each element's stable id and current listener events, and takes no borrow across render_immediate.

Handler coverage reads every screen the replays reach (boot and after each step), the overseer's delegate call (P4 Q2), held PROVISIONAL until the epoch boundary; the canvas handler count is deferred to 0.4.0, and the stopPropagation limit is opened as a residual row.

Handler coverage's stated limits: handlers inside a canvas are not counted, a handler on no screen a replay reached is not listed, and a bubbling dispatch counts every ancestor listener it passed, a stopPropagation unread.

body:
The session added a third role to the escher-session command line: coverage <app> <check>... replays one or more kept check files and prints one JSON line listing the UI graph's handlers no check exercised.
The line's form is {"unexercised":[{"id","owner","event"}],"checks":n,"held":m}, owner left out when absent, hand-written, uncoloured; endings stay the four statuses (0 accepted, 1 refused malformed, 2 usage, 3 session error), none added.
In-process it adds escher_driver::handler_coverage with Coverage and HandlerRef, and in the DOM bridge a reached-handler record (ReachedHandler, record_reached, reached_handlers) written on the handle_event path.
It adds the stand_handler_coverage target (8 tests) and a stand_replay test replaying a kept actions step; run stand reads 262 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored over 54 files.
docs/capabilities.md gains three limits: handlers inside a canvas are not counted, a handler on no screen a replay reached is not listed, a bubbling dispatch counts every ancestor listener it passed.
No verb, schema, MCP, socket, dependency or spec-master change; nothing retired.
The subjects list of design-system's items (the comment naming palette through web-spa-canvas) must gain a cli-coverage item for the new coverage role's output.

The cli Component Patterns rule that escher-session, the driver's command line and its mcp role are agent-read surfaces now covers a third role, coverage; any text naming the role set as the command line plus mcp alone is stale.
The cli-output rule (stdout holds only JSON, one line per command, never colour or an ESC byte, no terminal test) holds for the coverage role as well: one uncoloured JSON line on stdout.

The exit-status classes 0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error are reused by the coverage role unchanged and none is added; a malformed check file is refused with status 1, a wrong argv shape is usage 2, a failing boot is 3.
The command line's usage line gains the clause coverage role: coverage <app> <check>... before the apps clause; any cli item quoting the usage line or its role clauses is reached.

The cli Navigation Pattern NOT YET MEASURED note (no slice recorded argument parsing or command structure for the CLI binaries) is reached: the session defines a closed argv shape for the coverage role, an app then one or more check paths, no --session and no --record word.

The cli-graph item is reached indirectly: the coverage reader reads the UI graph at boot and after each replayed step (mounted left out, deduplicated by id and event) to find each handler a screen shows.
The cli-actions item is reached indirectly: a kept check's actions steps now replay under test, and the coverage role replays kept checks of any step kind.
The web-spa canvas surface is reached by a stated limit: handlers dispatched inside a canvas element's one listener are not counted by handler coverage, deferred to 0.4.0.
Any count of escher-driver crate-root re-exports moves 59 to 62 (Coverage, HandlerRef, handler_coverage), and of dioxus-native-dom re-exports 35 to 36 (ReachedHandler).
Any stand inventory or reading moves: stand files 53 to 54, run stand 244 passed over 52 files to 262 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored over 54 files; stand_replay tests 3 to 4.
Any CLI test inventory moves: seven_guis cli_commands 17 to 18 on linux, escher-driver cli_tests 5 to 6, json tests 7 to 8, the line table 102 to 109 rows, host_log 5 to 6.

The coverage line holds ids, owner ids, event names and two counts only; a typed value never reaches it and a refusal holds nothing of the check file's path or bytes, which bears on any cli rule about what output carries.

body_fields.fact: The escher-session coverage role (coverage <app> <check>...) prints one uncoloured JSON line {"unexercised":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"event":…}],"checks":n,"held":m}, owner left out when absent, listing the UI graph handlers no given kept check exercised; it ends 0 accepted, 1 malformed, 2 usage or 3 session error, adding no exit status.

The coverage role reads each named check file bounded at 1,048,576 + 1 bytes and refuses malformed, status 1, any file it cannot read, past the bound, not a check, or a check of another app, the refusal holding nothing of the path or the file.

Handler coverage has three stated limits: handlers inside a canvas are not counted, a handler on no screen a replay reached is not listed, and a bubbling dispatch counts every ancestor listener it passed with stopPropagation unread.

body:
Added a third escher-session command-line role, coverage <app> <check>..., that reads kept-check files the caller names on argv and prints one JSON line listing the UI graph handlers no check exercised.
Each path is read under a byte bound (MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1, 1,048,576 + 1) through the strict Check::from_bytes; an unreadable, over-bound, non-check or other-app file is refused malformed (status 1) holding nothing of the path; a boot failure is status 3, usage status 2, accepted status 0.
Added escher_driver::handler_coverage, Coverage and HandlerRef (crate re-exports 59 to 62), and in dioxus-native-dom an ungated reached record (ReachedHandler, record_reached, reached_handlers, re-exports 35 to 36) written on the bridge's handle_event path beside the SignalRegistry dispatch.
The coverage line holds ids, owner ids, event names and two counts only; a typed sentinel never reaches it, and host_log reads no id, name, path or check content at trace; no new span, log site, verb, dependency, socket or MCP surface.
Discharged the owed kept actions replay test named for Handler coverage (stand_replay gains a_kept_actions_step_replays_and_a_changed_one_stops_naming_nodes); the founder ratified kept-check files on the role's argv as a boundary widening.
Retired nothing; VERBS stays fourteen, info_span sites stay 2, Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock byte-identical.

CLI arguments (escher-session) rule: command_line gains the coverage role, the only role that reads files named on argv; still the four fixed endings 0/1/2/3, nothing the caller typed written back, a --session or --record word among the paths is usage; the usage line gains a coverage role clause.

Recorded check (Check::from_bytes) rule: a kept check now has a second reader, the command line's coverage role, reading caller-named files under the byte bound and refusing malformed with nothing of the path or file; every replayed step still passes validate inside Session::run.
Committed checks exception: the strict reader is now reached from the command line too; the two committed Counter checks themselves are byte-unchanged and stay the one exception to owner-only.
Kept checks file medium: a kept check may now be named to escher-session coverage; of it only ids, owner ids, event names and counts reach stdout, never its steps, typed text or path.

Threat model CLI input vector: a new entry point, escher-session coverage reading arbitrary local files the caller names, an untrusted input bounded and parsed strictly; the attack surface list names only example and rdme CLI entry points today.
Data-protection fact naming Handler coverage as the owner of the owed actions replay test (the discharged entry, fct-cl72c3yo): the test now exists and passes, so the CARRY is discharged.

Dioxus bridge rule (fct-frlob5k5 and its detail, fct-3atajnay): holds as written for the SignalRegistry dispatch, and gains the reached record beside it on handle_event, active only where record_reached was called; every other document pays one has_context lookup per dispatch.
Stable element id carriers: ids now also leave through the coverage answer line (ids and owner ids), still no NodeId crossing.
Stdout output fact: escher-session writes a new line form on stdout, the coverage line {unexercised:[{id,owner,event}],checks,held}, uncoloured, holding nothing the caller typed.
Refusal and SessionError format: the coverage role reuses the malformed cause (Refusal::new(Cause::Malformed)) and the fixed SessionError table; no new cause, the eight-cause set unchanged.
Widening rule and ratified widenings: kept-check files named on the role's argv are a ratified boundary widening (pattern rul-izni57qv) on the founder's word relayed by the overseer (inputs#I4, Q1).
Driver command schema: VERBS stays fourteen verbs; the coverage line is no verb, no Outcome variant and no node key; the command line still routes every replayed call through validate.
serde_json dependency fact: still a reader only; Coverage::to_json is hand-written and serde_json writes nothing; no dependency added.
Environment values read: escher-driver's unit tests reaching target/tmp through CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR now include the coverage role test's scratch files; no new env read.

Logging: no new span or log site; each replayed step leaves its own command span through Session::run, info_span sites in escher-driver stay 2; host_log gains a sixth test reading the coverage run at trace.

Test and count citations: stand files 53 to 54, run stand 262 passed 0 failed 7 ignored over 54 files, stand_replay 3 to 4, cli_commands linux 17 to 18, host_log 5 to 6, cli_tests 5 to 6, json tests 7 to 8, the line table 102 to 109 rows, any security fact citing these moves.
